title: De institutione musica (15th c. MS)
shelf_note: A 15th-century Latin manuscript of Boethius on music fits the OPenn/UPenn collections. The 'americana' collection tag looks odd for this text but is harmless.
structure_note: The structure count says pages_translated 0, but the book field says 106 and this page has a translation, so one of the counters is wrong (E2). There are 49 'printed numbers' in a manuscript with no folio visible on this leaf, plus 4 backsteps and 2 repeats. These are probably marginal numerals or chapter numbers read as page numbers, not a real disorder.

ocr_errors.problem: The text says hammer 12 to hammer 9 (the 4:3 fourth), but the transcription reads 12 to 8, which is a 3:2 ratio. That breaks the arithmetic of the proportion.
The numerals of the tone ratio are swapped. The ratio is the same either way.
'cyathos' (ladlefuls) is misread as 'quatuor' (four), and the translation turns it into 'four cups'
The transcription is garbled ('ferreaue percutiens'). The translator reconstructed it correctly.

missing.why: A general reader will not know who Albinus is: a Roman writer on music whom Boethius cites, and whose work is lost.

book_verdict: The page and its translation are mostly sound, and the notes are good glosses. But a numeral misread (12:8 for 12:9) carried into the English makes the fourth's ratio wrong, and several word misreads (cyathos, acumen, gravitas) weaken the passage on voice limits.
